course.title: Dance Fitness
course.tagline: Get fit dancing Afrobeats and more, with routines that burn and entertain.

days.title: Your first dance workout
days.goal: Do your first dance workout and have fun moving.

video.title: 30 Minute Dance Workout at Home | Afro Dance Cardio, Standing, No Jumping

steps: Clear a small space and put on shoes that grip well.
Watch the video and follow the easy moves.
Move at your own pace and rest when you need to.
Drink water and write down how you felt.
days.task: Finish the dance workout and write how you felt.
days.challenge: Do the workout again tomorrow.

quiz.q: What do you need for a dance workout?
options: A small clear space and good shoes
quiz.explain: Space and shoes are enough to start.

quiz.q: What should you do if you miss a step?
options: Keep moving and join in again
quiz.explain: Missing a step is normal; keep going.

quiz.q: Why drink water during dance?
quiz.explain: Water keeps you cool and strong.

days.title: Warm up with a groove
days.goal: Learn a warm-up that gets you moving to music.
steps: March in place to the music for 1 minute.
Roll your shoulders and sway your hips.
Step side to side and clap on the beat.
Reach your arms up and breathe in.
days.task: Do the warm-up before every dance workout.
days.challenge: Teach the warm-up to a friend.

quiz.q: Why warm up before dancing?
options: It wakes up muscles and lowers injury risk
quiz.explain: A warm-up gets the body ready to move.

quiz.q: How long should a warm-up take?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is enough.

quiz.q: What is a good warm-up move?
quiz.explain: Marching to music wakes the body up.

days.title: Learn the Afrobeats bounce
days.goal: Learn the basic bounce that drives Afrobeats dance.
steps: Stand with knees soft and bounce gently to the beat.
Let your shoulders and arms move with the bounce.
Step side to side while keeping the bounce.
Add a small hip sway.
days.task: Bounce to one song for 2 minutes.
days.challenge: Add side steps to your bounce.

quiz.q: What is the Afrobeats bounce?
options: A gentle knee bounce to the beat
quiz.explain: The bounce is the base of Afrobeats dance.

quiz.q: What should your knees do?
quiz.explain: Soft knees keep the bounce smooth.

quiz.q: Why keep the bounce small?
options: Small moves are easier to control
quiz.explain: Small, controlled moves keep you steady.

days.title: Step touch and grapevine
days.goal: Learn two classic dance steps.

video.title: 5-6000 Steps Walk To The Beat | 60 Min Dance-Fit GOLD

steps: Step touch: step to the side, touch the other foot next to it.
Grapevine: step side, cross behind, step side, touch.
Do each step slowly first, then to music.
Add arm swings as you step.
days.task: Do 10 step touches and 10 grapevines.
days.challenge: Do both steps to music for 2 minutes.

quiz.q: What is a step touch?
options: Step to the side, touch the other foot next to it
quiz.explain: A step touch is a simple side step.

quiz.q: What is a grapevine?
options: Step side, cross behind, step side, touch
quiz.explain: A grapevine weaves the feet side to side.

quiz.q: Why learn steps slowly first?
quiz.explain: Slow first, fast later is the safe way.

days.title: Move your hips and shoulders
days.goal: Learn simple hip and shoulder moves.

video.title: 20 Min Afrobeats Dance Workout for Beginners

steps: Sway your hips side to side to the beat.
Roll your shoulders back in a circle.
Combine hips and shoulders together.
Keep your knees soft the whole time.
days.task: Do hip sways for 1 minute to music.
days.challenge: Combine hips and shoulders for 1 minute.

quiz.q: Why keep knees soft while dancing?
options: It is a rule with no reason
Soft knees protect joints and keep moves smooth
quiz.explain: Soft knees absorb the bounce.

quiz.q: What is a shoulder roll?
options: Rolling the shoulders back in a circle
quiz.explain: A shoulder roll loosens the upper body.

quiz.q: How should hip moves feel?
quiz.explain: Smooth, relaxed moves are safe.

days.title: Cardio dance: keep moving
days.goal: Do a 10-minute dance workout that raises your heart rate.
steps: Warm up for 5 minutes.
Dance for 10 minutes using the steps you know.
Rest for 1 minute, then dance 5 more minutes.
Cool down with slow walking.
days.task: Dance for 10 minutes without stopping.
days.challenge: Dance for 15 minutes tomorrow.

quiz.q: What is cardio dance?
options: Dancing that raises your heart rate
quiz.explain: Cardio dance trains the heart through dance.

quiz.q: How should cardio dance feel?
options: Warm and breathing faster, but able to talk
quiz.explain: Warm but talkable is the right effort.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end?
quiz.explain: A cool-down slows the body gently.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Your first dance routine
days.goal: Put week 1 together: build a short dance routine.

video.title: Afro Dance Party Workout at Home

steps: Pick 4 moves you know: bounce, step touch, grapevine, hip sway.
Put them in order: 8 counts each.
Practise slowly, then to music.
Do the routine 3 times.
days.task: Write your routine and do it 3 times.
days.challenge: Do your routine to a full song.

quiz.q: What is a dance routine?
options: Moves put in order to music
quiz.explain: A routine links moves together.

quiz.q: How many moves should your first routine have?
quiz.explain: Four moves is enough to learn.

quiz.q: Why practise slowly first?
quiz.explain: Slow first, fast later is safe.

project.title: Your first dance routine
project.brief: Build a short dance routine with 4 moves: bounce, step touch, grapevine and hip sway, 8 counts each, and do it 3 times.

days.title: Belly dance basics
days.goal: Learn gentle belly dance moves for fitness.
steps: Try a hip lift: lift one hip up, then the other.
Try a chest lift: lift your chest up and down.
Try a small shimmy: shake your hips fast and small.
Keep your knees soft and breathe normally.
days.task: Do hip lifts for 1 minute.
days.challenge: Try a small shimmy for 30 seconds.

quiz.q: What is a hip lift?
options: Lifting one hip up, then the other
quiz.explain: A hip lift is a basic belly dance move.

quiz.q: What is a shimmy?
options: A fast, small shake of the hips or shoulders
quiz.explain: A shimmy is a quick shake.

quiz.q: Why keep knees soft?
options: It is a rule with no reason
quiz.explain: Soft knees keep moves safe.

days.title: Zumba basics: easy steps
days.goal: Learn the simple steps used in Zumba.

video.title: Dance-Fit GOLD: Low Impact Dance Fitness

steps: Try the salsa step: forward, back, side, side.
Try the merengue march: march in place with hip sways.
Try the cumbia step: step back and sway.
Do each step for 1 minute to music.
days.task: Do the salsa step for 1 minute.
days.challenge: Do all 3 steps to one song.

quiz.q: What is Zumba?
options: A dance workout using Latin steps
quiz.explain: Zumba is dance fitness with Latin music.

quiz.q: What is the salsa step?
quiz.explain: The salsa step is a basic Zumba move.

quiz.q: What should you do if you miss a step?
options: Keep moving and join in again
quiz.explain: Missing a step is normal; keep going.

days.title: Dance walk: steps for weight loss
days.goal: Learn a dance walk that burns energy gently.
steps: Walk in place to music with arm swings.
Add side steps and knee lifts.
Add a small turn every 8 counts.
Walk for 10 minutes.
days.task: Dance walk for 10 minutes today.
days.challenge: Dance walk for 15 minutes tomorrow.

quiz.q: What is a dance walk?
options: Walking to music with dance moves added
quiz.explain: A dance walk mixes walking and dance.

quiz.q: Why is dance walking good for weight loss?
options: It burns energy gently for a long time
quiz.explain: Gentle, long movement burns energy.

quiz.q: What should you add to a dance walk?
quiz.explain: Arms and knees make the walk a full workout.

days.title: Learn a new Afrobeats move
days.goal: Add one new Afrobeats move to your routine.
steps: Watch the video and pick one move you like.
Break it down: feet first, then arms, then together.
Practise slowly 10 times.
Add it to your routine.
days.task: Learn one new move today.
days.challenge: Add the new move to your routine.

quiz.q: How should you learn a new move?
options: Feet first, then arms, then together
quiz.explain: Breaking it down makes learning easy.

quiz.q: How many times should you practise?
quiz.explain: Slow repeats build the move.

quiz.q: What should you do if a move is hard?
options: Slow down and break it smaller
quiz.explain: Smaller pieces make hard moves doable.

days.title: Dance for your legs
days.goal: Use dance moves that build leg strength.
steps: Do squats to the beat: 8 squats, rest, repeat.
Do side lunges to the beat.
Do calf raises: rise on your toes to the beat.
Keep your knees with your toes.
days.task: Do 2 rounds of 8 squats to music.
days.challenge: Do calf raises for 1 minute to music.

quiz.q: What do dance squats build?
quiz.explain: Squats to music build legs.

quiz.q: What is a calf raise?
quiz.explain: A calf raise trains the lower legs.

quiz.q: What should your knees do in a squat?
options: Point the same way as your toes
quiz.explain: Knees following toes keeps the squat safe.

days.title: Dance for your core
days.goal: Use dance moves that work your middle.
steps: Do standing twists: twist your waist side to side.
Do knee lifts: lift each knee to your chest.
Do hip circles: circle your hips slowly.
Keep your belly tight as you move.
days.task: Do standing twists for 1 minute.
days.challenge: Do knee lifts for 1 minute to music.

quiz.q: What is your core?
options: The muscles around your belly and lower back
quiz.explain: Core muscles hold your body steady.

quiz.q: What does a standing twist work?
quiz.explain: Twists work the waist.

quiz.q: Why keep your belly tight?
options: It is a rule with no reason
quiz.explain: A tight belly steadies the body.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your 20-minute dance workout
days.goal: Put week 2 together: build a 20-minute dance workout.
steps: Warm up for 5 minutes.
Dance for 10 minutes using your routine.
Add a dance walk for 5 minutes.
Cool down with slow walking and stretching.
days.task: Write your 20-minute workout and do it.
days.challenge: Do your workout twice this week.

quiz.q: What should a 20-minute workout have?
options: Warm-up, dance, dance walk and cool-down
quiz.explain: A full workout warms up, works and cools down.

quiz.q: How long should the dance part be?
quiz.explain: Ten minutes of dancing is a good workout.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end?
quiz.explain: A cool-down slows the body gently.

project.title: Your 20-minute dance workout
project.brief: Build a 20-minute dance workout: warm-up, 10 minutes of dancing, a 5-minute dance walk, and a cool-down.

days.title: Learn a full Afrobeats routine
days.goal: Learn a full Afrobeats dance routine step by step.

video.title: 20 MIN DANCE WORKOUT At Home | Zumba Class

steps: Watch the video and learn the first 8 counts.
Add the next 8 counts.
Put the whole routine together slowly.
Dance it to music 3 times.
days.task: Learn the first 8 counts today.
days.challenge: Dance the full routine to music.

quiz.q: How should you learn a routine?
quiz.explain: Small chunks make learning easy.

quiz.q: What is a count in dance?
quiz.explain: Counts help you stay on the beat.

quiz.q: How many times should you practise?
quiz.explain: Repeats to music build confidence.

days.title: Dance with a friend
days.goal: Dance with a friend and have fun together.

video.title: Zumba Inspired Walk For Weight Loss

steps: Invite a friend to dance with you.
Teach them your favourite move.
Dance your routine together.
Cheer each other on.
days.task: Dance with a friend this week.
days.challenge: Teach a friend your favourite move.

quiz.q: Why dance with a friend?
options: It makes it fun and keeps you going
quiz.explain: A friend adds fun and keeps you honest.

quiz.q: What should you teach a friend first?
quiz.explain: An easy move is a good first teach.

quiz.q: What should you do after dancing together?
quiz.explain: Cheering keeps a friend coming back.

days.title: Low-impact dance for everyone
days.goal: Learn dance moves that are gentle on the joints.
steps: Keep one foot on the floor at all times.
Use small steps and soft knees.
Avoid jumps and fast spins.
Dance for 10 minutes gently.
days.task: Dance low-impact for 10 minutes today.
days.challenge: Teach low-impact moves to an older relative.

quiz.q: What is low-impact dance?
options: Dance with one foot on the floor at all times
quiz.explain: Low-impact dance is gentle on joints.

quiz.q: Who is low-impact dance good for?
quiz.explain: Low-impact suits all ages.

quiz.q: What should you avoid in low-impact dance?
quiz.explain: Jumps and fast spins strain joints.

days.title: Cool down with slow dance
days.goal: Learn a slow cool-down dance.

video.title: 30 Minute Dance Workout at Home | Afro Dance Cardio, Standing, No Jumping

steps: Slow the music down.
Sway gently side to side.
Stretch your arms up and breathe out.
Walk slowly for 2 minutes.
days.task: Do a slow cool-down dance after your workout.
days.challenge: Teach the cool-down to a friend.

quiz.q: Why cool down after dancing?
options: It slows the heart rate gently
quiz.explain: A cool-down lets the body calm down.

quiz.q: What is a good cool-down move?
quiz.explain: Gentle sways calm the body.

quiz.q: How long should a cool-down take?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is enough.

days.title: Dance and balance
days.goal: Use dance to improve your balance.
steps: Stand on one leg for 10 seconds while swaying.
Do slow turns with your arms out.
Step forward and back on a line.
Keep your eyes on one spot.
days.task: Stand on each leg for 20 seconds.
days.challenge: Do slow turns with arms out.

quiz.q: Why does dance help balance?
options: It trains you to shift weight smoothly
quiz.explain: Dance builds balance through weight shifts.

quiz.q: What helps you balance in a turn?
options: Looking at one spot and arms out
quiz.explain: A still gaze keeps you steady.

quiz.q: What should you do if you wobble?
quiz.explain: Wobbling is normal; try again.

days.title: Make your own dance mix
days.goal: Build a playlist for your workouts.
steps: Pick 5 songs you love with a clear beat.
Order them: slow warm-up, fast middle, slow cool-down.
Dance to your mix for 20 minutes.
Share your mix with a friend.
days.task: Build your 5-song workout mix.
days.challenge: Dance to your mix this week.

quiz.q: Why build your own mix?
options: Music you love makes you want to move
quiz.explain: Loved music keeps you dancing.

quiz.q: How should you order your mix?
options: Slow warm-up, fast middle, slow cool-down
quiz.explain: Slow-fast-slow matches the workout.

quiz.q: How many songs should your mix have?
quiz.explain: Five songs cover a 20-minute workout.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Your dance show
days.goal: Put week 3 together: prepare a short dance show.

video.title: 5-6000 Steps Walk To The Beat | 60 Min Dance-Fit GOLD

steps: Pick your best routine and your best song.
Practise the routine 5 times this week.
Perform it for a friend or family member.
Ask them what they liked best.
days.task: Practise your routine 5 times this week.
days.challenge: Perform your routine for someone.

quiz.q: What should your show have?
options: Your best routine and your best song
quiz.explain: Your best routine and song make a good show.

quiz.q: How many times should you practise?
quiz.explain: Practice builds confidence.

quiz.q: What should you ask your audience?
quiz.explain: Asking what they liked builds confidence.

project.title: Your dance show
project.brief: Prepare a short dance show with your best routine and song, practise 5 times, and perform it for a friend or family member.

days.title: Test your fitness
days.goal: Test how much fitter you have become.

video.title: 20 Min Afrobeats Dance Workout for Beginners

steps: Count how long you can dance without stopping.
Count how many squats you can do to music.
Check your heart rate after dancing.
Write all three numbers down.
days.task: Record your 3 test numbers today.
days.challenge: Beat one number next week.

quiz.q: Why test your fitness?
options: To see how much fitter you have become
quiz.explain: Tests show progress in numbers.

quiz.q: What should you do if a number is lower?
options: Keep dancing and test again in 2 weeks
quiz.explain: Numbers go up and down; steady dancing brings them up.

quiz.q: How often should you test?
quiz.explain: A few weeks apart shows real change.

days.title: Dance for joy, not just fitness
days.goal: Remember why you dance: joy matters too.
steps: Dance to your favourite song just for fun.
Try a silly move and laugh.
Dance with your family.
Write down why you love dancing.
days.task: Dance to your favourite song for fun today.
days.challenge: Write why you love dancing.

quiz.q: Why dance for joy?
options: Joy keeps you dancing for life
quiz.explain: Fun keeps the habit alive.

quiz.q: What should you do when dancing feels like a chore?
options: Play your favourite song and dance for fun
quiz.explain: Fun music brings the joy back.

quiz.q: Why write down why you love dancing?
options: So you remember on hard days
quiz.explain: Your own words remind you why you started.

days.title: Keep dancing every week
days.goal: Make dance a weekly habit.

video.title: Afro Dance Party Workout at Home

steps: Dance 3 times a week, even if short.
Join a local dance class or group.
Set a new goal: learn a new routine.
Write your weekly dance plan.
days.task: Write your weekly dance plan.
days.challenge: Dance 3 times this week.

quiz.q: How often should you dance?
quiz.explain: Three times a week keeps the habit alive.

quiz.q: Why join a dance group?
quiz.explain: A group adds fun and keeps you honest.

quiz.q: What is a good next goal?
quiz.explain: A new routine keeps you growing.

days.title: Learn a salsa basic step
days.goal: Learn the basic salsa step.
steps: Step forward with your left foot, then back to the middle.
Step back with your right foot, then back to the middle.
Keep your knees soft.
Move your hips gently with each step.
Add arm moves once the feet feel easy.
Practise with slow music.
days.task: Do the salsa basic step for 2 minutes.
days.challenge: Do it to a full song.

quiz.q: What is the salsa basic step?
quiz.explain: The basic step moves forward and back in rhythm.

quiz.q: Why keep your knees soft?
quiz.explain: Soft knees let you step smoothly.

quiz.q: When should you add arm moves?
quiz.explain: Feet first, arms later keeps learning simple.

days.title: Dance fitness with a chair
days.goal: Learn a seated dance workout for days you are tired.

video.title: Dance-Fit GOLD: Low Impact Dance Fitness

steps: Sit tall in a sturdy chair.
March your feet to the music.
Raise your arms up and down.
Twist gently side to side.
Tap your toes to the beat.
Do it for 10 minutes.
days.task: Do the chair dance for 10 minutes.
days.challenge: Do it every day this week.

quiz.q: Why use a chair?
options: So you can dance even when you are tired
quiz.explain: A chair lets anyone dance, even on a tired day.

quiz.q: What should the chair be?
quiz.explain: A sturdy chair keeps you safe while dancing.

quiz.q: How long should the chair dance last?
quiz.explain: Ten minutes is a good gentle workout.

days.title: Film your dance routine
days.goal: Learn to film yourself dancing to check your moves.
steps: Set your phone on a table.
Press record and dance your routine.
Watch the video and pick one move to fix.
Practise that move 5 times.
Film again and compare.
Share the video with a friend if you like.
days.task: Film your dance routine today.
days.challenge: Fix one move and film again.

quiz.q: Why film yourself dancing?
options: To see your moves and fix them
quiz.explain: Video shows what you cannot feel while dancing.

quiz.q: What should you look for in the video?
quiz.explain: Fixing one move at a time works best.

quiz.q: Where should you put your phone?
options: On a table or stand, steady
quiz.explain: A steady phone gives a clear video.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final show.
steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 moves you can now do well.
Practise your capstone routine once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 moves you can do well now.
days.challenge: Do your capstone routine from memory.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final show that proves what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can dance your routine smoothly from memory
quiz.explain: A smooth routine shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone once more, then rest.
steps: Dance your capstone routine one more time.
Check your music and your space.
Fix anything that felt rushed.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Dance your capstone routine and time it.
days.challenge: Fix one thing that felt rushed.

quiz.q: Why practise once more?
options: Practice makes the real show calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your music, your space and your moves
quiz.explain: Checking music and space makes the show smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you perform your best.

days.title: Capstone day: your dance show
days.goal: Show what you learned: perform your dance routine.
steps: Warm up for 5 minutes.
Perform your routine to music for a friend or family.
Cool down with slow walking and stretching.
Write a short report on how it went.
days.task: Perform your dance show and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: What is the first step of your show?
quiz.explain: A warm-up gets the body ready.

quiz.q: What matters most in the show?
options: Going as fast as you can
Smooth moves, good rhythm and joy
quiz.explain: Smooth, joyful dancing shows real skill.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: What you performed and how it felt
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Your dance show
capstone.brief: Perform your dance routine to music for a friend or family member, with a warm-up and cool-down, and write a short report on how it went.
deliverables: A short video or notes from the show
